audit.title: Direct Funding Method

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opening: "This method doesn't require a subscription and is optimal for one-off requests for randomness." Section leads are mostly self-contained. Minor: "Limits" opens by deferring to another page rather than stating a canonical limit.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; clean H1→H2→H3, 0 level skips, all 6 sections under 156 words — ideal RAG chunk sizes. No tables where the parameter list and limits would benefit from one.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Mixed. 22 numerals but 0 carry units, and key numbers (min/max confirmations, `maxNumWords`, gas overhead) are all delegated to the Supported Networks page rather than stated. Parameters are named but not quantified inline.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 8 links to canonical Solidity source (`VRFV2PlusWrapper.sol`, `VRFCoordinatorV2_5.sol`, `LinkToken.sol`) plus an Etherscan verified-contract example. One opaque "here" link.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. EOA and direct-funding both get crisp, liftable one-liners. The direct-funding-vs-subscription contrast is well phrased for extraction.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, missing canonical, absent datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. No freshness signal for engines to trust.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 fenced code blocks. The page walks through `fulfillRandomWords`, `requestRandomness`, and `calculateRequestPrice` in prose but shows no actual Solidity, forcing an agent to leave the page to complete the task.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Adequate. Covers concept → setup → processing → limits, but has no troubleshooting/FAQ section and no symptom- or error-phrased entry points.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming of Wrapper/Coordinator/service, no undefined jargon, unambiguous. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured conceptual overview of Chainlink VRF v2.5's direct funding method, strong on primary-source citations (8 links to canonical contract source on GitHub) and clear terminology. Its two biggest GEO weaknesses are structural to the page type: it contains **zero code blocks** despite instructing developers to "set up your contract," and it exposes **no machine-readable metadata** (no JSON-LD, canonical, or last-updated). The single highest-lift opportunity is adding a runnable consumer-contract snippet and a limits/parameters table, which would let engines synthesize the setup steps they currently can only paraphrase from prose.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal runnable direct-funding consumer contract
recommendations.where: "Set up your contract and request" section
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks; steps like "implement the `fulfillRandomWords` function" are prose-only.
recommendations.change: Add a complete, tagged ` ```solidity ` snippet importing `VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase`, showing `pragma solidity ^0.8.x`, a constructor with the wrapper address, `requestRandomness(...)` with all four named params, and a `fulfillRandomWords` override. Label the network.
recommendations.why: Coding agents read docs to complete tasks; a self-contained snippet is the single most citable/liftable artifact for a "how do I request VRF with direct funding" query.

recommendations.title: Add a limits/parameters table with concrete values
recommendations.issue: "The minimum and maximum confirmations for your network can be found here" — all numbers deferred offsite.
recommendations.change: Add a table listing each parameter (`requestConfirmations`, `callbackGasLimit`, `numWords`, `extraArgs`) with its type, purpose, and at least one concrete example value (e.g. Ethereum Mainnet `maxNumWords`, `maxGasLimit`). State `callbackGasLimit ≤ maxGasLimit - wrapperGasOverhead` with an example.
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes; a table lets engines extract limits without following a link that retrieval may not resolve.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical URL and dateModified
recommendations.issue: Measured facts show 0 JSON-LD, missing canonical, absent dates.
recommendations.change: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a canonical `url`. Surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for agents; note this is largely a template-level fix, not page-authored.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: new section near the end, plus rephrase existing H3s
recommendations.issue: Headings are concept-titled ("How VRF processes your request"); no error/how-do-I phrasing.
recommendations.change: Add Q-phrased entries: "When should I use direct funding instead of a subscription?", "How much LINK do I need to fund the contract?", "Why can't I send a VRF request directly from my wallet (EOA)?" — the last already answered verbatim in body text but not discoverable by that query.
recommendations.why: Devs and agents query by symptom/intent; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present.

recommendations.title: Lead the "Limits" section with a canonical statement
recommendations.issue: "You can see the configuration for each network on the Supported networks page."
recommendations.change: Open with the invariant: "Each VRF v2.5 Wrapper enforces two limits: `maxNumWords` (max random values per request) and `callbackGasLimit ≤ maxGasLimit − wrapperGasOverhead`." Then defer per-network values.
recommendations.why: A self-contained first sentence survives chunking and defends against retrieval that never reaches the linked page.

recommendations.title: Fix the opaque "here" link
recommendations.issue: Opaque anchor text carries no entity signal.
recommendations.change: Replace with "found on the [Supported Networks page](/vrf/v2-5/supported-networks)."
recommendations.why: Descriptive anchor text improves link-target entity resolution and citation quality.

antiPatterns: Instructional page ("set up your contract") with no code snippets — an agent-runnability gap.
Numbers delegated wholesale to a linked page rather than stated inline (weakens standalone chunk value).
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and og/twitter tags are template/site-level concerns; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata can be fully verified rather than inferred absent.
The page already references `/llms.txt` — good site-level discoverability signal; ensure this page is listed there.
Per-network numeric values live on the Supported Networks hub; strengthen internal linking so this page is reachable from that hub (canonical-hub pattern).
